historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored mid-cycle (FY27 organic flat, FY27-29 'close to the lower end of +3% to +6%' on average), decelerating to 2.0% terminal; the trailing CAGRs straddle the FY2023 peak (revenue 12,137) and the FY2026 trough (9,404) and are not a usable forward proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-yr equity CAGR (-0.4%) diverges from 3-yr revenue (-8.1%) and EPS (-18.5%) CAGRs by more than 30%: FY2023 was the post-COVID/China-reopening peak and FY2024-FY2026 is a destocking downcycle, so the 3-yr window measures peak-to-trough, not trend. 5-yr figures (revenue +1.3%, equity +1.9%, EPS -0.9%) are the better through-cycle read and are roughly flat.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC) FY2021 1,538 -> FY2023 1,287 -> FY2026 1,172. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.1pp of each other: SBC is immaterial (0.2-0.4% of revenue) and the house/street band is narrow. FY2026 FCF was flattered by trough capex (391 vs 667/773 in FY25/FY24).

scenario_narratives.base: Pernod is a scale spirits owner (Absolut, Jameson, Martell, Chivas, Ballantine's, Royal Salute, Malibu, Beefeater, Havana Club, Perrier-Jouet/Mumm) whose cash flows are set by three axes: US premium-spirits demand after the 2021-22 pull-forward, China/travel-retail cognac demand (Martell is the largest profit pool and the most cyclical), and the India/Rest-of-World growth engine. The base case takes management at its word on FY27 (organic flat, with US and China still destocking in H1 and underlying China trends improving), then recovers to the low end of the +3-6% medium-term range through FY29-FY30 before fading to 2% nominal. EBITDA margin rebuilds from the FY26 trough (27.4%, after EUR 261m of restructuring/impairment) to a mid-cycle 29.5% as the EUR 1bn FY26-FY28 efficiency programme is partly reinvested in 16% A&P. Capex and ageing-stock investment stay within the 'strategic investments <= EUR 700m' envelope; cash conversion ~90% is consistent with the component build. Leverage (3.6x ND/EBITDA) is carried through the net-debt bridge, not the discount rate; management's <3x FY29 target is achievable on these flows while maintaining the EUR 4.70 dividend.
scenario_narratives.bull: US inventory normalises by mid-FY27 and sell-out stabilises; China cognac demand recovers with the EU-China duty settlement and Martell regains share; India (Blenders Pride, Royal Stag, Jameson) and Africa/LatAm compound high-single-digit; FY28-FY30 organic growth of 5-6% at the midpoint of the range. The efficiency programme lands in full with restructuring charges ending FY28, taking margin back to the FY2022 peak of ~31.5% by FY32. Lower capex (5%) as the Irish whiskey and cognac capacity programmes complete. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The US spirits category is in structural decline (moderation, GLP-1s, RTD/cannabis substitution) and tariffs on EU spirits are passed through at the cost of volume; China cognac never returns to 2019-2023 levels and EU-China duties stay in place; travel retail stagnates. FY27 reported revenue -5%, then a sub-2% nominal grind with margin stuck at 26-26.5% as efficiencies are spent on price and A&P defence and restructuring becomes semi-permanent. Higher capex (6%) as ageing-stock commitments cannot be cut quickly. Net debt/EBITDA stays above 3.5x, keeping the equity geared to the cycle. Terminal growth 1.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on a leveraged, cyclical premium-spirits franchise. The valuation does not capitalise the FY2026 trough (margin 27.4%, capex 4.2%) nor the FY2022 peak (31.2%): the base case rebuilds to a 29.5% EBITDA margin on a 5.5% capex and negative working-capital-capture basis, consistent with the FY2017-FY2026 average and the EUR 1bn efficiency programme net of brand reinvestment. Leverage is charged once, through the EUR 10.2bn ex-lease net debt in the bridge; NCI is deducted at book; leases are an operating cost (treatment B). Because the business grows at roughly the discount rate minus 5pp, the 15% hurdle entry price sits well below intrinsic value - that is the price of demanding 15% from a 7%-WACC asset, not a signal that the model disagrees with itself.
key_risks_to_valuation: US spirits demand: ~27% of net sales; a structural (not cyclical) decline in premium spirits consumption would push the bear path.
China/cognac: Martell is the largest single profit pool; EU-China anti-dumping duties on cognac and weak Chinese consumer confidence drive both the FY24-26 decline and any recovery.
Leverage: EUR 10.2bn net debt (3.6x EBITDA) against ~EUR 17bn market cap; each 1pp of EBITDA margin is ~EUR 95m of EBITDA and ~EUR 2.5-3/share of equity value through the bridge.
FX: ~70% of sales outside the eurozone, USD and CNY largest; a weaker USD is a direct reported-EUR headwind that organic guidance does not cover.
Working capital/ageing stock: 85% of EUR 7bn+ inventories are ageing whisky and cognac; a demand miss cannot be met by cutting the stock build quickly, so FCF lags revenue on the way down.

Terminal value share: with a 7% WACC and 2% terminal growth, roughly 55-60% of EV sits in the terminal; the 18x cap binds in the base case, so terminal_growth sensitivity is muted but the cap multiple itself is the judgment.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (RI.PA) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 57.86-88.42 EUR
data_sources.financials: RI.PA_Metrics.csv / core_metrics FY2017-FY2026 (EUR m) derived from the Universal Registration Documents; FY2026 URD (year ended 30 June 2026) for the balance sheet, cash flow statement, lease notes, share count and FY27 / FY27-29 outlook (section 5.4)
data_sources.qualitative: RI.PA_Analysis.json not yet available at build time; scenario axes taken from the FY2026 URD outlook and management commentary (US/China inventory adjustments, EUR 1bn efficiencies, 16% A&P, <3x ND/EBITDA by FY29, strategic investments <= EUR 700m) and the H1 FY2026 half-year report.

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares FY2026 (252,342,140; URD FY2026 note 'Earnings per share'); 252,269,195 shares issued less 456,633 treasury = 251.8m basic. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks have fallen to ~EUR 10m/yr (anti-dilution only) while the group deleverages.
inputs.sbc_source: URD FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' add-back EUR 16m (FY2025: 25m). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis); Pernod settles performance shares from treasury stock.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built. Risk-free 3.3% (10y OAT, Oct-2026), ERP 5.5%, beta 1.05 (spirits is staples-labelled but US/China/travel-retail demand and cognac inventory cycles make it behave cyclically) -> cost of equity ~9.1%. Pre-tax cost of debt 3.4% (company's own weighted average cost of debt FY2026, URD note 'Weighted average cost of debt'), ~2.5% after tax. Target structure ~65/35 equity/debt (ND/EBITDA 3.6x today, management targets <3x by FY29) -> 6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the flows and the weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full FY2026 lease cash cost (EUR 101m principal in financing + EUR 20m lease interest in operating = EUR 121m, 1.3% of revenue) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (EUR 449m) are EXCLUDED from net debt (net debt ex-leases 10,213 per URD section 5.3). D&A is taken ex right-of-use depreciation (413 - 140 = 273, 2.9% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests deducted at book (EUR 1,040m at 30 June 2026; NCI share of profit EUR 36m, ~3% of net profit). Flows are left consolidated. Book is the more conservative of book (1,040) and capitalised NCI profit (~650 at 18x).
inputs.equity_bridge_note: Investments in associates (EUR 63m) added because the share of associates' result (-1m) is outside the EBITDA flows. The EUR 1,098m of non-current financial assets is left out of the bridge (largely guarantee deposits, loans and pension-related items whose income is not separable in the flows) - a conservative omission of at most ~EUR 4/share.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: reported_fcf 1,188 = OCF 1,579 - capex 391, which is AFTER interest paid (465) and received (65) because Pernod classifies both in operating activities. last_fcf = 1,188 - 16 SBC = 1,172 (levered owner FCF, the anchor the dashboard reads). interest_income is 0 by rule: this is a EUR 10.2bn net-debt company, so the cash is netted inside net debt and its interest is simply part of net finance cost. The projection is UNLEVERED (component build from EBITDA, discounted at WACC, net debt deducted), so year-1 unlevered owner FCF (~1,380) sits above last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest bill (~345); the two reconcile.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer'), 10-year horizon, with the adaptations file applied: EUR-built WACC, single lease treatment (B), NCI charged once in the bridge, risk charged once. Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. Mid-cycle vs peak-cycle: FY2026 EBITDA margin 27.4% (recurring 30.2% before EUR 261m of other operating expenses, mainly Fit-for-Future restructuring and impairments) is near the bottom of the FY2017-FY2026 range (27.2%-31.2%, mean ~29%); base path recovers to 29.5% by year 5 as the EUR 1bn FY26-FY28 efficiency programme lands net of 16% A&P and continuing restructuring, i.e. a mid-cycle margin, not the FY2022 peak. FY2026 capex of EUR 391m (4.2%) is a trough and is NOT carried forward: base capex 5.5% of revenue (~EUR 520m rising to ~EUR 670m), inside the 'strategic investments <= c. EUR 700m' guidance once ageing-stock build is counted. Working capital: 85% of inventories are ageing whisky/cognac stocks, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture -35% on the revenue change (and FY2026 still consumed EUR 241m on falling sales, which the 5.5% capex allowance partly absorbs). Cash tax 26%: FY2026 ETR 28%, cash paid 21% of PBT, French statutory 25.8% with a lower-rate mix outside France. FY27 growth is REPORTED EUR growth: organic broadly stable per guidance, less a residual FX/scope headwind (weak USD, Imperial Blue and wine disposals annualising).

bear.growth_rationale: US spirits volumes keep falling (moderation, GLP-1s, RTD/cannabis substitution, tariff pass-through), China cognac demand does not recover and EU-China cognac duties persist; FY27 reported -5% (organic -3%, FX/scope -2%), then a sub-2% nominal grind.
bear.margin_rationale: Efficiencies are absorbed by price investment and A&P defence; restructuring becomes semi-permanent; margin stuck around 26-26.5%, below the FY2017 trough-of-range 27.2%.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 organic flat per guidance less ~1pp residual FX/scope; FY28-FY29 at ~3-4% (the low end of the +3-6% medium-term range, which with a flat FY27 averages ~2.3% over FY27-29, a touch below management's 'close to the lower end'); fades to 2.0% nominal by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: 27.5% in FY27 (FY26 27.4% with restructuring charges continuing under the EUR 1bn programme), +0.5pp/yr to 29.5% by FY31 = the FY2017-FY2026 mean plus ~0.5pp for efficiencies net of 16% A&P. Below the FY2022 peak of 31.2%.

bull.growth_rationale: US and China destocking completes in FY27 and both markets return to growth in FY28; India and Rest of World keep compounding high-single-digit; FY28-FY30 at the middle of the +3-6% range.
bull.margin_rationale: Full EUR 1bn efficiency capture with restructuring charges ending FY28; margin back to the FY2022 peak of ~31.5% by FY32.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: three consecutive years of organic decline (FY24 -1%, FY25 -3%, FY26 -3.9%), the US and China - the two largest profit pools - are both in inventory correction with a plausible structural overlay (moderation, GLP-1s, cognac duties, US tariffs), and 3.6x leverage magnifies any further earnings slide. Bull cut to 25%: it needs US sell-out, China cognac and full efficiency capture to all come right at once, and management itself has guided to the LOW end of its medium-term range.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
